content.title: About
content.content: The cookie, chocolate and vanilla sandwich consists of two soft cookies with a creamy filling flavored with chocolate and vanilla. It is a popular quick dessert often sold in packs of 2–4 pieces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate sandwich appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
The chocolate‑vanilla flavor pairing is one of the most beloved combinations in confectionery.
Cookies are often lightly glazed to preserve a crisp texture.
Some markets add a pinch of sea salt to enhance the flavor profile.
The product is convenient for on‑the‑go consumption: it does not require refrigeration and keeps its shape for several days.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Cocoa in the chocolate filling is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Dairy ingredients in the cream can contribute to bone health.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which may improve mood.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: Milk and egg components add a modest amount of protein.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Contains milk, eggs, and gluten, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A serving (2–4 pieces) can contain 200–350 kcal.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Some versions may include partially hydrogenated oils.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sandwich as a standalone treat, crumble it into ice cream, use it as a filling for ice‑cream sandwiches, or simply pair it with a cup of coffee or tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package. At temperatures above 25 °C the cream may soften and the cookies lose their crunch. Follow the “best before” date printed on the packaging.
